questionText: What is the primary purpose of inter-VLAN routing?
options: Forward traffic between different IP networks associated with VLANs
Assign MAC addresses to switch ports
explanation: Inter-VLAN routing provides Layer 3 communication between IP subnets associated with separate VLANs.

questionText: Which device can perform inter-VLAN routing?
explanation: A Layer 3 switch supports IP routing and can route between VLANs using switched virtual interfaces.

questionText: What does router-on-a-stick use to route traffic between VLANs?
options: One physical router interface with multiple 802.1Q subinterfaces
A separate physical router for every VLAN
A wireless controller without IP routing
explanation: Router-on-a-stick uses router subinterfaces with 802.1Q encapsulation over a trunk link to route among VLANs.

questionText: Which Cisco IOS subinterface command identifies VLAN 20 for an 802.1Q router-on-a-stick connection?
explanation: The encapsulation dot1Q 20 command on a router subinterface associates that subinterface with tagged traffic from VLAN 20.

questionText: Which command enters configuration mode for router subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0.10?
explanation: The interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 command selects a logical subinterface on the physical router interface.

questionText: A router-on-a-stick implementation serves VLANs 10 and 20. What mode should the connected switch port normally use?
explanation: The switch interface connecting to a router-on-a-stick router normally operates as an 802.1Q trunk to carry the VLANs.

questionText: Which Cisco IOS global configuration command enables IPv4 routing on a supported multilayer switch?
explanation: The ip routing command enables IPv4 packet routing on supported Layer 3 switches.

questionText: A Layer 3 switch uses VLAN 10 with subnet 192.168.10.0/24. Which logical interface is commonly assigned the gateway address 192.168.10.1?
explanation: An SVI configured as interface vlan 10 can serve as the default gateway for hosts on the VLAN 10 subnet.

questionText: Host A is 192.168.10.50/24 in VLAN 10, and Host B is 192.168.20.50/24 in VLAN 20. Which gateway settings are appropriate if a Layer 3 switch has SVI addresses .1 in each subnet?
options: Host A uses 192.168.10.1 and Host B uses 192.168.20.1
Neither host requires a gateway for inter-VLAN traffic
explanation: Each host must normally use a reachable gateway in its own local subnet: 192.168.10.1 for VLAN 10 and 192.168.20.1 for VLAN 20.

questionText: Which command displays the IPv4 routing table on a Cisco router or Layer 3 switch?
explanation: The show ip route command displays the IPv4 routing table, including connected and learned routes.

questionText: What type of route normally appears when an operational Layer 3 SVI is configured with an IP address and prefix?
options: A directly connected route for the SVI subnet
A BGP route to every VLAN
A default route to the Internet
explanation: An operational SVI with an IP address normally creates a connected route for that subnet in the routing table.

questionText: A switch SVI for VLAN 30 is configured with an IP address and no shutdown, but its line protocol remains down. What should be checked?
options: Whether VLAN 30 exists and has an eligible active forwarding Layer 2 port
Whether DNS can resolve the switch hostname
Whether the console cable is connected
Whether a remote website uses HTTPS
explanation: An SVI commonly requires an active VLAN and a qualifying Layer 2 port in a forwarding state to bring its line protocol up.

questionText: A router-on-a-stick setup has working VLAN 10 connectivity, but VLAN 20 hosts cannot reach their gateway. The router has a VLAN 20 subinterface. Which trunk issue is most relevant?
options: VLAN 20 is missing from the switch trunk's allowed VLAN list
The router hostname differs from the switch hostname
The console speed is set to 9600 baud
The switch uses a different management DNS server
explanation: If VLAN 20 is excluded from the trunk, tagged frames for VLAN 20 cannot reach the corresponding router subinterface.

questionText: Which statement about a Layer 3 switch SVI and a router subinterface is correct?
options: Both are always physical Ethernet ports
Both can provide Layer 3 gateway services for VLAN-associated subnets
Neither can have an IP address
Both require DTP negotiation with clients
explanation: SVIs and router subinterfaces are logical Layer 3 interfaces that can provide default-gateway connectivity for VLAN subnets.

questionText: A router-on-a-stick trunk uses native VLAN 99. Which Cisco IOS subinterface encapsulation command marks VLAN 99 as native?
explanation: On supported router subinterfaces, encapsulation dot1Q 99 native associates untagged native-VLAN traffic with VLAN 99.

questionText: When a router forwards an IPv4 packet from VLAN 10 to VLAN 20, what normally happens to the packet's Ethernet header?
options: It is retained unchanged end to end
It is removed and a new outgoing Layer 2 header is created
It is copied into the DNS query
It is permanently converted into a TCP header
explanation: Routing removes the incoming Layer 2 encapsulation and creates an appropriate new Layer 2 header for the outgoing interface or VLAN.

questionText: A PC needs to send an IP packet to a host on another VLAN and subnet. Which destination MAC address does it normally put in the outgoing Ethernet frame?
options: The local default gateway's MAC address
The switch console port's MAC address
The broadcast address in every case
explanation: For an off-subnet destination, the PC sends the frame to the MAC address of its local next-hop gateway.

questionText: A multilayer switch has SVIs for VLAN 10 and VLAN 20, both up, with correct IP addresses. Hosts can ping their own gateways but not hosts in the other VLAN. Which setting should be verified first?
options: Whether the switch's console password is encrypted
Whether all ports use the same native VLAN
explanation: Without IPv4 routing enabled on a multilayer switch, operational SVIs alone may provide local gateway reachability without forwarding traffic between subnets.

questionText: A router uses GigabitEthernet0/0.10 for VLAN 10 and GigabitEthernet0/0.20 for VLAN 20. The parent GigabitEthernet0/0 interface is administratively shut down. What is the likely result?
options: Both subinterfaces are unable to pass traffic through the shut-down parent interface
Traffic automatically moves to the console port
VLAN 10 traffic becomes untagged on every switch
explanation: Router subinterfaces depend on their parent physical interface. An administratively down parent prevents normal data forwarding.

questionText: Which Cisco IOS interface command changes a supported Layer 3 switch Ethernet port from a Layer 2 switchport to a routed port?
explanation: The no switchport interface command turns a supported multilayer switch interface into a Layer 3 routed port.

questionText: Two VLANs use subnets 192.168.10.0/24 and 192.168.20.0/24. A Layer 3 switch has active SVIs for both and IP routing enabled. What additional routing protocol is required solely to route between these connected networks?
options: No dynamic routing protocol is required
explanation: The switch can route directly between its connected SVI subnets without requiring a dynamic routing protocol.

questionText: A router subinterface uses encapsulation dot1Q 40, while the connected switch sends the intended user traffic tagged as VLAN 50. What is the problem?
options: The VLAN tags do not match the router subinterface encapsulation
The router needs a different hostname
802.1Q does not support VLAN IDs above 30
The IP addresses must be public
explanation: Traffic tagged for VLAN 50 will not be processed as VLAN 40 traffic by a subinterface configured for dot1Q VLAN 40.

questionText: What is one important advantage of inter-VLAN routing on a capable Layer 3 switch compared with a router-on-a-stick design?
options: It eliminates the need for VLAN IDs
It can route between SVIs without sending every inter-VLAN packet over one external router trunk
It requires separate physical routers for each subnet
explanation: A multilayer switch can route between local VLAN interfaces internally, avoiding the single external router trunk used by router-on-a-stick.

questionText: VLAN 10 uses 10.10.10.0/24 with gateway 10.10.10.1. A host is configured as 10.10.10.50/24 with gateway 10.10.20.1. What is the most direct problem?
options: Its default gateway is outside the host's local subnet
Its host address is a broadcast address
Its VLAN number must match the last IP octet
explanation: The configured gateway 10.10.20.1 is outside 10.10.10.0/24, so the host normally cannot reach it as an on-link next hop.

questionText: A Layer 3 switch successfully routes between VLANs 10 and 20, but policy requires VLAN 10 hosts to reach a server in VLAN 20 only on TCP port 443. What additional feature can enforce this restriction?
options: A Layer 3/4 access control list applied appropriately
explanation: An appropriately placed extended ACL can filter inter-VLAN traffic by IP addresses, transport protocol and port number.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of Spanning Tree Protocol in an Ethernet switched network?
options: Increase the number of VLAN IDs
explanation: STP prevents Layer 2 switching loops by placing selected redundant paths into nonforwarding states while retaining backup connectivity.

questionText: Which IEEE standard originally defined Spanning Tree Protocol?
explanation: IEEE 802.1D originally defined STP for bridged Ethernet networks.

questionText: Which device is elected as the central reference point of an STP topology?
explanation: STP elects a root bridge, and the other participating switches calculate their best paths toward that root.

questionText: How is the root bridge selected in STP?
explanation: The switch with the lowest bridge ID becomes the STP root bridge.

questionText: Which components determine the ordering of STP bridge IDs?
options: Bridge priority information and MAC address
Number of VLANs and optical power
explanation: Bridge ID comparison is based on priority information, including the extended system ID where applicable, followed by the bridge MAC address.

questionText: Two switches compete to be root bridge. Both have the same effective bridge priority, but Switch A has bridge MAC 0011.2233.4455 and Switch B has 0011.2233.4466. Which becomes root?
options: The switch with the higher IP address
explanation: With equal priority components, the lower bridge MAC address wins. 0011.2233.4455 is lower than 0011.2233.4466.

questionText: What is the root port on a nonroot STP switch?
options: The port with the best path toward the root bridge
The port with the largest MAC address
A port that always remains disabled
explanation: A nonroot switch selects a root port providing its best STP path toward the root bridge.

questionText: How many root ports does a nonroot switch normally have per spanning-tree instance?
options: None, because only roots have root ports
explanation: A nonroot bridge normally selects one root port for a given spanning-tree instance.

questionText: Which statement about ports on the STP root bridge is correct?
options: The root bridge always has one root port
The root bridge has no root port
Every root bridge port is automatically blocked
The root bridge has no designated ports
explanation: The root bridge is the reference point for the spanning tree and does not select a root port.

questionText: Which port role represents the port selected to forward traffic from a shared network segment toward the root?
explanation: A designated port is the selected forwarding port for its segment and advertises the best path to the root on that segment.

questionText: What does BPDU stand for?
explanation: BPDUs are Bridge Protocol Data Units exchanged by bridges and switches for spanning-tree operation.

questionText: What information do STP switches use BPDUs to exchange?
options: Root and path information used to establish the loop-free topology
explanation: BPDUs convey spanning-tree information including root identity and path information to support elections and topology decisions.

questionText: Which classic 802.1D STP port state forwards ordinary user data?
explanation: The forwarding state allows normal user frames to be sent and received through the switch port.

questionText: Which classic STP state learns source MAC addresses but does not yet forward ordinary user frames?
explanation: In the learning state, a switch builds its MAC address table but does not yet forward normal user traffic.

questionText: What is the default hello time for classic IEEE 802.1D STP?
explanation: The default STP hello timer is two seconds.

questionText: What is the default forward-delay timer used by classic 802.1D STP?
explanation: The default forward-delay timer is 15 seconds, used for the listening and learning intervals during classic STP convergence.

questionText: What is the default max-age value in classic STP?
explanation: The default STP max-age timer is 20 seconds.

questionText: Which IEEE standard introduced Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol (RSTP)?
explanation: IEEE 802.1w introduced Rapid Spanning Tree Protocol, which provides faster convergence than classic 802.1D STP in many scenarios.

questionText: What is a major benefit of RSTP compared with classic STP?
options: Faster convergence after many topology changes
Guaranteed removal of all physical link failures
explanation: RSTP can respond more quickly to topology changes through improved port roles and convergence procedures.

questionText: Which three port states are used by RSTP?
explanation: RSTP uses three operational states: discarding, learning and forwarding.

questionText: What is the purpose of an RSTP alternate port?
options: Provide an alternate path toward the root bridge
explanation: An alternate port offers a backup path toward the root bridge and normally remains in discarding state until needed.

questionText: What is the purpose of an RSTP backup port?
options: Provide a backup for a designated port on the same shared segment
Replace the root bridge's MAC address
explanation: An RSTP backup port provides a redundant connection to a segment for which the same switch already has a designated port.

questionText: Which Cisco IOS command displays spanning-tree status and the current root bridge information?
explanation: The show spanning-tree command displays information such as root identification, port roles, costs and states.

questionText: Which Cisco IOS command configures a switch as the preferred root for VLAN 10 using Cisco's root-primary macro?
explanation: The spanning-tree vlan 10 root primary command adjusts bridge priority to make the switch a preferred root for VLAN 10, subject to topology and platform behavior.

questionText: With the extended system ID used on a typical Cisco Catalyst switch, which is a valid configurable STP bridge-priority value?
explanation: Cisco bridge priorities using the extended system ID are configured in increments of 4096. The value 4096 is valid.

questionText: Switch A has STP priority 4096 and Switch B has priority 8192 in the same spanning-tree instance. Assuming no lower-ID bridge participates, which switch is elected root?
options: The switch with more access ports
The switch with the higher interface speed
explanation: Lower effective bridge priority wins before MAC address comparison, so Switch A becomes root.

questionText: What is the intended use of PortFast on a Cisco switch?
options: Allow suitable host-facing ports to transition quickly to forwarding
Make the switch root for every VLAN
explanation: PortFast allows eligible edge ports to transition rapidly to forwarding rather than waiting through classic STP delays. It should be used on appropriate edge connections.

questionText: Which interface command traditionally enables PortFast on a suitable Cisco access port?
explanation: The spanning-tree portfast interface command enables PortFast on supported Cisco switch ports.

questionText: What is the primary purpose of BPDU Guard on a PortFast-enabled edge port?
options: Protect against an unexpected switch connection by disabling the port when a BPDU is received
explanation: BPDU Guard can place a protected edge port into an error-disabled state if it receives a BPDU, helping prevent unintended Layer 2 topology connections.

questionText: An access port with PortFast and BPDU Guard enabled receives a BPDU from an accidentally connected switch. What normally happens?
options: The port becomes the root port immediately
The port enters an error-disabled state
The port becomes a trunk automatically
The switch disables its management SVI
explanation: On typical Cisco Catalyst behavior, BPDU Guard detects the unexpected BPDU and error-disables the protected interface.

questionText: What is the purpose of Root Guard on a Cisco switch port?
options: Prevent a downstream device from becoming root through that port
Allow any superior BPDU to replace the root immediately
Disable IPv4 routing on the switch
Change every port to access mode
explanation: Root Guard prevents an unexpected downstream bridge from taking over as root by placing the affected port into a root-inconsistent state when superior BPDUs arrive.

questionText: What is the purpose of Loop Guard in a Cisco spanning-tree deployment?
options: Prevent selected non-designated ports from incorrectly transitioning to forwarding after BPDUs stop arriving
Turn a trunk into a DHCP server
Elect the switch with the highest MAC address
Allow Layer 2 loops to improve redundancy
explanation: Loop Guard helps prevent alternate or root ports from becoming designated and forwarding incorrectly when expected BPDUs are lost.

questionText: A nonroot switch has two paths toward the same STP root bridge. Path A has total root path cost 8 and Path B has total root path cost 19. Which path is preferred, assuming both are valid?
options: Neither path can become a root path
explanation: STP prefers the lower total root path cost, so Path A with cost 8 is preferred over Path B with cost 19.

questionText: A nonroot switch receives two otherwise equivalent BPDUs advertising the same root and equal total root path cost, but the sending bridge IDs differ. Which BPDU is preferred for root-port selection?
options: The one with the lower sender bridge ID
The one with the higher sender bridge ID
The one arriving on the port with the highest VLAN ID
The one with the larger Ethernet frame length
explanation: When root ID and total path cost tie, STP compares the sending bridge ID and prefers the lower value before further tie-breakers.

questionText: A redundant switch-to-switch link fails while RSTP is running. What can RSTP do when a suitable alternate path already exists?
options: Rapidly transition an alternate port toward forwarding after the appropriate convergence process
Convert the remaining links to half duplex
explanation: RSTP can activate an eligible alternate path more quickly than classic STP when topology conditions permit rapid convergence.
